title: sb add --help creates worktree instead of showing help
description: Running 'sb add --help' creates a worktree named '--help' and a branch 'feat/--help' instead of displaying help text. Subcommands need basic flag parsing to handle --help and -h before treating the argument as a worktree name.

title: Add input validation for pathological branch/worktree names
description:
Add aggressive input validation to reject pathological worktree/branch names:
- Names starting with dash (-)
- Names with path traversal (../, ./)
- Names with shell metacharacters ($, `, |, ;, &, etc.)
- Empty names or whitespace-only
- Names that are git reserved (HEAD, refs/, etc.)
- Excessively long names
- Names with null bytes or control characters
Fail fast with clear error messages.

title: Add sb doctor command for health checks
description: Add 'sb doctor' command that checks: stale worktree refs, misplaced worktrees, worktrees/ in .gitignore, orphan branches. Similar to 'bd doctor' pattern. Should suggest fixes.

title: sb remove cannot handle names starting with dash
description: Running 'sb remove --foo' tries to remove worktree named '--' not '--foo'. Need to support '--' separator or better argument parsing for names starting with dashes.

title: Add --json output mode for agent consumption
description: Add '--json' flag to list/audit commands for machine-parseable output. Agents need structured data for programmatic worktree management. Format: {worktrees: [{name, path, branch, status}]}

title: Add sb detect command for aq interlock
description: Add 'sb detect' command that outputs current worktree context (branch, repo remote, worktree path) in a format aq can consume. This closes the gap in build step 6 (sb detect → aq announce). Currently sb list shows all worktrees but there is no command to detect and emit the CURRENT worktree's identity. Output should be parseable: JSON by default or with --json flag. Example: sb detect → {"worktree": "feat/my-feature", "remote": "github.com/jwalsh/aq", "path": "worktrees/my-feature", "agent": "github.com/jwalsh/aq/feat/my-feature"}. This enables: aq announce -c C-1 --claim "..." --worktree $(sb detect --field worktree).

title: sb detect should feed agent identity to aq
description: Protocol Gap #12 showed that agent identity tied to git remote+branch causes monorepo pathology (co-located agents invisible to each other). sb detect should generate agent identity from worktree path, not just remote+branch. When multiple agents share a worktree, sb detect --agent-id should incorporate a disambiguator (PID, ULID, or explicit --agent-id flag). This prevents the self-exclusion bug where aq's checkConflicts skips broadcasts from the same agent address.

title: Document validate vs check separation for users
description: Cross-worktree validation revealed user confusion: aq validate checks protocol health (ULID uniqueness, timestamps, well-formedness), aq check detects file/concept overlap. Users expect validate to catch conflicts. Add clear documentation distinguishing the two. sb's role: sb doctor checks worktree health (analogous to aq validate), sb audit checks placement (analogous to aq check for spatial violations).
